title: Repair and Emergency Service Calls — Late-Payment Charge Calculation Standard
content:
## Collections standard

**1. When a charge is owed.** A late-payment charge is owed on a completed call under Repair and Emergency Service Calls whose balance is still owing, once more than the late-payment grace of 30 days (the call class's figure) has passed since its completion date. Late-payment days are counted as calendar days with the completion date as day 0. The completion date and the balance are read from the call record.

**2. Period and rate.** The charging period is 30 days. The rate is the call class's late-payment charge of 1.5 percent for each charging period.

**3. Counting periods.** Once the grace has passed, one charging period is counted for the first day past the grace, and one more for each further full charging period.

**4. One line for all uncharged periods.** The charge for every period counted and not yet charged is posted together as one late-payment charge line on the invoice.

**5. Periods already charged.** Periods already charged are the periods counted, in the same way, as of the posting date of the call's latest late-payment charge line. Only the periods counted beyond them are charged now.

**6. Amount.** The late-payment charge is the balance owing on the call on the day it posts, multiplied by the rate in percent and by the number of periods being charged now. It is rounded once at the end to the cent half up, and it is never less than the call class's minimum late-payment charge of 2 dollars. An amount that falls exactly halfway between two cents is rounded up to the higher cent; for this purpose an amount within 1e-09 of a dollar below the half cent counts as exactly halfway.

**7. No charge.** Where no period is left to charge, or nothing is owing on the call, no late-payment charge is posted.

## Period count by days since completion (30-day grace)

| Days since completion | Days past the grace | Periods counted |
|---|---|---|
| 30 | 0 | None |
| 31 | 1 | 1 |
| 60 | 30 | 1 |
| 61 | 31 | 2 |
| 90 | 60 | 2 |
| 91 | 61 | 3 |

## Worked example (hypothetical call)

**First charge.** The call is completed on 2 March (day 0) with $412.00 owing. On 15 May the call is at day 74, which is 44 days past the grace, so 2 periods are counted. No late-payment charge line exists yet. The charge is $412.00 multiplied by 1.5 percent and by 2, which is $12.36, posted as one line.

**Second charge.** Later, at day 100, the call is 70 days past the grace and 3 periods are counted. As of the latest charge line, posted at day 74, 2 periods had been counted. One period is charged now, on the $424.36 then owing: $6.3654, rounded to $6.37.

**Minimum.** A balance of $90.00 with one period to charge gives $1.35, so the charge posted is $2.00.
